scope: Standalone uncached/MMIO store transport and local prepared-store fault consumer. No production IQ/ROB wiring, retirement/trap controller, data-port arbiter, cache, LSQ or full-core acceptance. No exhaustive formal, deadlock-freedom or physical timing claim.
launch: launch_i is final descriptor acceptance, legal only with ready_o and shared with upstream consumption. Route nonfault uncached stores and all prepared store faults here; cacheable nonfault stores use committed_store. Preserve full 13-bit ROB identity and retain PC/instruction metadata upstream. A descriptor may launch only after every older store has been prepared as a nonfaulting cacheable store or has already launched here; ordering only descriptors already routed here is insufficient because any older unprepared store may fault and require this engine. Otherwise launch only at ROB head. A younger waiting descriptor must never block an older head operation. Local faults carry cause 6 or 7, trap_value=address and zero data/mask; uncached classification may be zero on faults. Nonfault SB/SH/SW descriptors already passed alignment/PMA checks, with naturally aligned exact address, size, word-relative strobe and already shifted/masked data. No same-cycle consume/refill.
authorization: A held nonfault descriptor requires issue_allowed_i, head_valid_i and exact head_id_i. issue_allowed_i must include global fatal/recovery eligibility, required older-memory ordering, conservatively drained committed stores and a shared-port grant bound to owner_id_o. authorize_o is the accepted grant pulse: that edge reserves the port until response completion or platform reset/fatal handling, and makes the next-cycle request irrevocable. A grant is not merely a sampled idle indication. The future arbiter records engine ownership; independently allocated four-bit IDs cannot identify the engine. Classification alone grants no side-effect permission.
request: Present only responses routed to this engine by the recorded port owner. Offer exactly one uncached write with exact address/size and word-lane data/strobe. Cached fields are zero. Valid and payload hold until request acceptance, reset or fatal, even when head/issue permissions change. Minimum response latency is one cycle; response-cycle turnover is prohibited. Bus ID advances only on a well-formed response, including access faults.
result: Only a well-formed response produces an external-write result. OK holds success with original descriptor metadata. ACCESS_FAULT holds cause 7, trap_value=exact address and zero write data/mask. Local prepared faults complete without authorization or a bus request. take_i consumes the result only on the future atomic solo retirement edge for success, or accepted precise trap boundary for fault; neither result visibility nor request acceptance is retirement. Any unexpected response while a result is held suppresses valid_o immediately and latches fatal, so no result acceptance/retirement can race a frozen fatal owner. Caller take must be qualified by current valid_o. No PRF write is required. Fault events must not advertise a committed memory write. The target must return ACCESS_FAULT only when it rejected the write without a device effect; uncertain or partial effects require fatal handling, not retry. This is a required future target contract, not proof of a connected device.
recovery: kill_i is qualified to this owner, not a blanket redirect. It cancels WAIT_HEAD and local-fault results and wins over authorization. Once authorized, irrevocable_o remains set through request stalls, response wait and either success or fault result consumption. Caller recovery must defer until that boundary; a postoffer fault cannot be canceled and replayed. Illegal postauthorization kill is a caller contract violation checked by assertion. By RTL inspection, cancellation is gated so it cannot retract the offered write or hide its result; assertion-disabled illegal-kill behavior is not claimed as tested. No automatic retries.
fatal: Sticky fatal_o retains first fatal_reason_o: 0 none, 1 unexpected response phase, 2 wrong ID, 3 protocol/reserved status, 4 any nonzero read payload. Priority is phase, ID, status, payload. Fatal suppresses ready/authorization/request/response/result channels and freezes owned state until reset. busy_o, owner_id_o and irrevocable_o remain visible while fatal. Global control must separately observe fatal, including a fatal with an empty engine.
reset: Reset suppresses channels and ownership views, clears state/ID/fatal, and requires the target to suppress pre-reset responses. A reset after authorization may interrupt a device write; this module does not guarantee completion or undo it. Recovery is not reset.
